title: Maps of finitely presented algebras over a directed colimit of rings come from a stage
statement: Let $(\Lambda,\le)$ be a directed set and $(R_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ a directed system of commutative rings (ring maps $R_\lambda\to R_\mu$ for $\lambda\le\mu$, the identity for $\lambda=\mu$, compatible with composition) with colimit $R=\varinjlim_\lambda R_\lambda$ in the category of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $\lambda\in\Lambda$ and let $A$, $A'$ be finitely presented $R_\lambda$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. For $\mu\ge\lambda$ put $A_\mu=A\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu$, $A'_\mu=A'\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu$ ($R_\mu$-algebras), and $A_R=A\otimes_{R_\lambda}R$, $A'_R=A'\otimes_{R_\lambda}R$; identify $A_\mu\otimes_{R_\mu}R=A_R$ and $A'_\mu\otimes_{R_\mu}R=A'_R$ by $(a\otimes r)\otimes r'\mapsto a\otimes\bar r r'$. (2) For every homomorphism of $R$-algebras $u:A_R\to A'_R$ there are $\mu\ge\lambda$ and a homomorphism of $R_\mu$-algebras $u_\mu:A_\mu\to A'_\mu$ with $u_\mu\otimes1_R=u$. (3) If $v,w:A\to A'$ are homomorphisms of $R_\lambda$-algebras with $v\otimes1_R=w\otimes1_R$, then $v\otimes1_{R_\mu}=w\otimes1_{R_\mu}$ for some $\mu\ge\lambda$.

proof.text: Work on the nonempty directed upper tail J of i. Define B(j) = A' tensor_S F(j), its transition maps f(j,k) = id tensor F(j,k), and q(j) = id tensor colimit.ι(j). Functoriality and colimit cocone naturality give compatibility and composition of these maps, verified on pure tensors. Tensor commutativity transfers the two clauses of directedColimitBaseChangeElementwise to this right-tensor convention: every element of A' tensor_S R is represented in B(j), and an element of B(j) mapping to zero becomes zero at a later stage.

proof.text: Use a finite polynomial presentation π : S[X_1,...,X_n] → A with surjective π and finitely generated kernel. Represent g(π(X_a)) at stages of B and take a common upper bound ν. Polynomial evaluation gives p : S[X_1,...,X_n] → B(ν) with q(ν) p = g π. Every member of a finite kernel-generating set maps to zero over R, hence vanishes at a later stage by step 1. A common later stage ω kills all relations. Transition-map composition and Ideal.span_le show ker π ≤ ker p_ω. AlgHom.liftOfSurjective factors p_ω through π, producing g_ω : A → B(ω), and surjectivity of π proves q(ω) g_ω = g. Empty sets of variables or relations are handled by the nonempty directed-tail common-upper-bound lemma.

proof.text: Restrict u to A using includeLeft, and apply the proved private factorization helper from step 2. The tensor-product lift of g_μ and includeRight defines an S-algebra map A tensor_S F(μ) → A' tensor_S F(μ); its value on 1 tensor r shows it commutes with F(μ), so it is an F(μ)-algebra map. On a pure tensor its composite to the colimit is u(a tensor 1) times (1 tensor t(r)), equal to u(a tensor t(r)) because u commutes with R. Tensor induction proves the commuting-square equation for all elements.

proof.text: For equality descent, evaluate the assumed equality on a tensor 1. Swap tensor factors to show 1 tensor (v(a)-w(a)) = 0. The elementwise theorem supplies a stage at which each difference vanishes. Finite presentation implies finite type, so choose a finite algebra-generating set and a common upper bound for its vanishing stages and i. Transition maps preserve the equalities. AlgHom.ext_of_adjoin_eq_top shows includeLeft composed with v and w agree at this stage. Multiplication by 1 tensor r and tensor induction then prove equality of the tensor maps. The empty generating set is covered by choosing an upper bound with i.

lean.statement: theorem exists_map_of_finitePresentation_colimit {Λ : Type v} [Preorder Λ] [IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)] (F : Λ ⥤ CommRingCat.{v}) [HasColimit F] (i : Λ) (A : Type w) (A' : Type z) [CommRing A] [CommRing A'] [Algebra (F.obj i) A] [Algebra (F.obj i) A'] [Algebra.FinitePresentation (F.obj i) A] [Algebra.FinitePresentation (F.obj i) A'] : let S := F.obj i let R := colimit F letI : Algebra S R := (colimit.ι F i).hom.toAlgebra letI : Algebra R (A ⊗[S] R) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra letI : Algebra R (A' ⊗[S] R) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (∀ u : (A ⊗[S] R) →ₐ[R] (A' ⊗[S] R), ∃ (μ : Λ) (h : i ≤ μ), letI : Algebra S (F.obj μ) := (F.map (homOfLE h)).hom.toAlgebra let t : F.obj μ →ₐ[S] R := { (colimit.ι F μ).hom with commutes' := fun s ↦ congrArg (fun f : F.obj i ⟶ colimit F ↦ f s) (colimit.w F (homOfLE h)) } letI : Algebra (F.obj μ) (A ⊗[S] (F.obj μ)) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra letI : Algebra (F.obj μ) (A' ⊗[S] (F.obj μ)) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra ∃ uμ : (A ⊗[S] (F.obj μ)) →ₐ[F.obj μ] (A' ⊗[S] (F.obj μ)), ∀ x : A ⊗[S] (F.obj μ), Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S A') t (uμ x) = u (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S A) t x)) ∧ (∀ v w : A →ₐ[S] A', Algebra.TensorProduct.map v (AlgHom.id S R) = Algebra.TensorProduct.map w (AlgHom.id S R) → ∃ (μ : Λ) (h : i ≤ μ), letI : Algebra S (F.obj μ) := (F.map (homOfLE h)).hom.toAlgebra Algebra.TensorProduct.map v (AlgHom.id S (F.obj μ)) = Algebra.TensorProduct.map w (AlgHom.id S (F.obj μ)))
